_comment: WHAT IS PLUGGED IN. Selects units from shared/inventory.json and gives each
one an address, a position and a set of tags. It does not describe the
hardware (that is the .qxf), the room ('venue' below names one in
shared/venues/), or what was measured on the night (calibration.json).
Looks reference TAGS, never fixture ids or names. That is what lets a look
built for these four heads run on a club rig with eight.
Addresses match events/despacio/patch_sheet.csv as the show ran. 'position'
is in millimetres, y up, origin at the room's front-left floor corner --
the same frame venue.json uses. A fixture with a position becomes a
geometry head, in file order.
These coordinates moved 4572 mm in x and z on 2026-08-07, when the room was
remodelled twice as long and twice as wide with the rig standing on a truss
frame in the middle of it rather than on the walls. NOTHING ABOUT THE RIG
MOVED: measure from venue.json's `truss` rectangle and the four heads are
still 500 mm inboard of the bar at each corner, and the two pinspots still
centred on two opposite sides. The origin is still the ROOM's corner, and
the room now begins 4572 mm further out.
'hold' pins a channel every single frame. Reset is held at 0 because this
fixture treats 250-255 as a hold-to-reset command, and a stuck LTP value
there once put every head into a permanent reset loop.
'beam_deg' overrides the .qxf's cone angle. The MJ-OS-018 profile claims 3
degrees and these read visibly wider than that in the room, so they are set
to 8 -- STATED 2026-08-08, not measured. Measure it if it matters: this is
not only cosmetic, because engine/safety.py sizes the beam's half-width at
range from it, so a wider number makes the crowd taper dim earlier. That is
the conservative direction, but it does change the show.
A position does NOT make a fixture a geometry head -- load_rig only builds
a head for something that has Pan AND Tilt. The pinspots are placed so the
previz can draw them; they take no head index and shift nobody's
calibration.
name: despacio

fixtures.name: Pinspot #1
fixtures.notes: Channel 0 is a mode selector, not a dimmer. Confirmed on hardware 2026-08-01: the usable band is 240-255 (RGBW On); the .qxf's 9-134 White Dimmer band does not behave as a dimmer. Holding it at 255 every frame means the fixture is always in RGBW mode and brightness comes entirely from the R/G/B/W channels, which do behave linearly. Held by channel NAME because no generic role fits a mode selector.

fixtures.name: Pinspot #2
fixtures.notes: See Pinspot #1. Same plane as the movers (y 2971), centred on its side of the truss, and set inboard by the same 500 mm they are -- stated 2026-08-07, not measured. If 'north/south' meant the OTHER pair of sides, swap x and z in both pinspots' positions and nothing else changes.
